summary.text: Ro Khanna is the Democratic incumbent for California's 17th District in Silicon Valley, serving his fifth term. A former attorney, university lecturer and Commerce Department official, he first ran for the seat in 2014, lost to then-Rep. Mike Honda, and defeated Honda in 2016. His House website lists him on the Armed Services and Oversight committees and as a member of the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

paragraphs.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1976 (September 13, per Wikipedia).
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1998 and a J.D. from Yale University in 2001.

Worked as an attorney; in 2009 President Barack Obama appointed him a deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Commerce, where he led trade missions. He left in 2011 to join the law firm Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati.

Taught as a visiting lecturer in economics at Stanford University (2012-2016) and taught law at Santa Clara University; published a 2012 book on American competitiveness, Entrepreneurial Nation. Ballotpedia also lists membership on the California Workforce Development Board.
Ran for the 17th District seat in 2014, losing to Rep. Mike Honda 51.8% to 48.2% in the general election, then defeated Honda in the 2016 general election.
Took office in January 2017 and is serving his fifth term, per his House website.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (ranking member of the Subcommittee on Cyber, Innovative Technologies and Information Systems), the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the U.S. and the Chinese Communist Party, and the Oversight and Accountability Committee, where he previously chaired the Environment Subcommittee.
